_note: Hand scansions that override the shared scanner (.github/scripts/scan_latin.py), keyed book.line; one sc string per reader word of that line, same format as the scanner. Add a line here only after scanning it by hand, and say why. Recurring scanner blind spots in Virgil: Greek eu (Eurus, Teucri) and initial Ae- split in two; consonantal i after a prefix (coniunx, iniuria, disiecit) read as a vowel; it prefers synizesis (Danaum, reliquias) over the ordinary reading.

1.16.why: Samō hīc: Virgil's famous hiatus — no elision across the pause; Samos has a short first syllable.

1.21.why: pŏpŭlum, lātē, rēgem; the scanner had po- and pu- long and late, regem short.

1.27.why: in-iū-ri-a: the second i is consonantal (in + ius).

1.30.why: rēliquiās with long first syllable (relliquiae); Danaum's -um and atque's -e elide. The scanner forced synizesis on reliquias instead.

1.38.why: Teu- is a diphthong (Teucri); the scanner split it into two shorts.

1.42.why: iăcŭlāta, with its -a elided into long ē; the scanner had ia- and cu- long.

1.43.why: dis-iē-cit: three syllables, the i consonantal after the prefix.

1.47.why: con-iunx: two syllables, the i consonantal.

1.85.why: Eu- of Eurus is the Greek diphthong; ūna elides into it.

1.92.why: Ae-nē-ae: three long syllables; the scanner split the initial diphthong and shortened -ne-.

1.96.why: Dănăūm in three syllables, oppetere's -e elided into Ō; the scanner preferred synizesis (naum) with a long Da-.

1.110.why: Eu- of Eurus is the Greek diphthong, and tris (accusative plural, -īs) is long; the scanner split E-u and shortened tris.

1.119.why: Trōĭa here is the adjective (Troius, -a), three syllables, nominative with short -a before gaza; the scanner made it two syllables with a long final.

1.128.why: Dis-iec-t(am) with consonantal i after the prefix, -am elided; Ae-nē-ae three long syllables. The scanner split Ae and shortened -ne-.

1.140.why: Eure: Greek diphthong Eu-, one long syllable, so vestras keeps its long -ās; the scanner split E-u and shortened vestras.

1.144.why: Cȳmŏthŏē (Greek Κυμοθόη), four syllables with o-e in hiatus, not the Latin diphthong oe; the scanner read -thoe as one syllable and lengthened -mo-.

1.170.why: Ae-nē-ās three long syllables, septem's -em elided into Ae-; the scanner split Ae and shortened -ne-.

1.172.why: Trō-ĕs, two syllables (Greek nominative plural, short -es before h), and hărēna; the scanner made Troes one syllable and lengthened ha-.

1.180.why: Ae-nē-ās: initial diphthong one syllable, -nē- long (opening spondee); the scanner split Ae and made a dactyl A-e-ne.

1.181.why: lātē is long in both syllables and pĕlăgō has two shorts; the scanner had late short and pela- long (cf. 1.21).

1.213.why: aena is trisyllabic a-ē-na here (as aenis in 1.295): lītŏ(re) ă-ē-nă lŏ-cant ă-lĭ-ī; the scanner took ae as a diphthong, made 'to' long and had no valid foot-1 otherwise.

1.220.why: Ae-nē-ās: initial diphthong Ae- one long syllable, -nē- long (Ae-ne | as nunc); the scanner split Ae and made a dactyl A-e-ne.

1.231.why: Ae-nē-ās: initial diphthong and long -nē- (quid mĕ-ŭs | Ae-nē | ās in | tē com...); the scanner split Ae and read A-e-ne as a dactyl.

1.232.why: Troes is two syllables (Trō-ĕs, Greek -es) and potuēre has short po-: quid Trō | ĕs pŏ-tŭ | ē-rĕ quĭ | bus tot | fū-nĕ-ră | pas-sis. The scanner made Troes one syllable and gave po- a long quantity.

1.249.why: Trōĭa is neuter plural (arma Troia) with short final -a, three syllables, as in 1.119; the scanner made it two syllables with a long final -a.

1.252.why: dis-iun-gi-mur: the i after the prefix is consonantal (dis + iungo), so dis | iun-gi-mur, not di-si-un; the scanner read it as a vowel and added a syllable.

1.257.why: Cȳ-thĕ-rē-ă (four syllables, rē long): Cy-the | rē-ă-mă | nent im..; the scanner made rea one syllable and gave the short ma- of manent a long quantity.

1.260.why: Ae-nē-an: initial diphthong Ae- and long -nē- (Ae-nē | an ne-que); the scanner split Ae and read A-e-ne as a dactyl.

1.284.why: Assăracī has short sa and ra (Ăs-să-ră | cī), and Phthia is two syllables with long i (Phthī-am); the scanner made sa and ra long and read Phthiam as one syllable.

1.290.why: sēcūra has long sē- and cū-, final -a short: ac-ci-pi | ēs sē | cū-ră-vŏ | ... ; the scanner had short se- and a long final -a on ra and a long vo- of vocabitur.

1.299.why: Teucris is two syllables (Teu-cris, eu the Greek diphthong, as Teucrorum 1.38); the scanner split Te-u and counted three. hos-pi-ti | o Teu | cris ne | fa-ti | nes-ci-a | Di-do; ne is long in the thesis, as the scanner also has it.

1.304.why: Teucros is two syllables (Teu-cros, long by nature as an accusative plural); the scanner split Te-u: ac-ci-pit | in Teu | cros a-ni | mum men | tem-que be | nig-nam.

1.305.why: Ae-nē-ās: initial Ae- one long syllable and -nē- long (At pi-us | Ae-nē | ās per | noc-tem | plū-ri-ma | vol-vens); the scanner split Ae and read A-e-ne as a dactyl.

1.314.why: sē-sē is the only fit: Cui mā | ter me-di | ā sē | sē tu-lit | ob-vi-a | sil-va, with the second se lengthened in the arsis at the hephthemimeral pause; the scanner made both se short and tu- long (tulit has short tu-).

1.316.why: Threïssa is three syllables (Thrē-is-sa): Spar-tā | nae vel | qua-lis e | quos Thre | is-sa-fa | ti-gat. With no lengthening anywhere; the scanner took Threissa as two syllables and had to lengthen -lis and e- of equos.

1.318.why: dē is long and mōre has long mō- (mos, moris); habilem has short ha-bi-: Nam-(que) u-me | ris de | mo-(re) ha-bi | lem sus | pen-de-rat | ar-cum. The scanner had de and mo short and ha-bi long.

1.330.why: The scanner's fit is correct (checked by hand); the entry is needed only because this line shares a unit with 1.332, which the scanner cannot fit, and a unit with an unresolved line receives no sc at all.

1.331.why: The scanner's fit is correct (checked by hand); the entry is needed only because this line shares a unit with 1.332, which the scanner cannot fit, and a unit with an unresolved line receives no sc at all.

1.332.why: Hypermetric line: locorumque ends in an elided -que (-que erramus, 1.333) so the line has fifteen syllables and the scanner cannot fit it. iāc-tē | mūr do-cĕ(ās) | īg-nā | rī ho-mi | num-que lo | cō-rum(que). doceas elides into Ignari.

1.333.why: The scanner's fit is correct (checked by hand); the entry is needed only because this line shares a unit with 1.332, which the scanner cannot fit, and a unit with an unresolved line receives no sc at all.

1.341.why: in-iū-ri-a: the second i is consonantal (in + ius), so in | iu-ri-a, not i-ni-u; the scanner read it as a vowel and added a syllable. Longa est elides (Longast): ger-mā | num fu-gi | ens Lon | ga(est) in | iu-ri-a | lon-gae.

1.343.why: con-iunx: the i is consonantal, so con | iunx, not co-ni-unx; the scanner read it as a vowel and added a syllable: Huic con | iunx Sy | chae-us e | rat di | tis-si-mus | a-gri.

1.372.why: prima is the ablative (prīmā, with origine), long -ma: O de-a | sī prī | mā re-pe | tens ab o | ri-gi-ne | per-gam. The scanner made pri- and -ma short and re-pe- long.

1.378.why: Ae-nē-ās: initial Ae- one long syllable and -nē- long (Sum pi-us | Ae-nē | ās rap | tos ex | hos-te Pe | nā-tes); the scanner split Ae and read A-e-ne as a dactyl.

1.383.why: Eu- of Euro is the Greek diphthong, one syllable (as Eurus 1.110): vix sep | tem con | vol un | dis Eu | ro-que su | per-sunt; the scanner split E-u.

1.415.why: Ip-sa Pa | phum sub | lī-mis a | bit sē | dēs-que re | vī-sit: sublīmis has long -lī- (līmen) and short -mis, sub- long before bl, and ăbit has a short a; the scanner read su-bli short-short, mis long and a long, a valid line with three wrong quantities.

1.421.why: Ae-nē-ās: initial diphthong one syllable, -nē- long (Mī-rā | tur mō(lem) | Ae-nē | ās mā | gā-li-a | quōn-dam); -lem elided into Ae-. The scanner split Ae into A-e and made a dactyl A-e-ne. With Ae- one syllable, ma- and ga- of magalia must both be long for the line to scan.

1.424.why: mō-lī-rī: all three syllables long (mōlior, mōlīrī), -que elided into ar- and -cem into et, then mănĭbus short-short: mo-li | ri ar | et ma-ni | bus sub | vol-ve-re | sa-xa. The scanner made li and ri short and ma and ni long.

1.438.why: Ae-nē-ās: initial diphthong one syllable and long -nē- (Ae-nē | ās a-it | et fas | tī-gi-a | sus-pi-cit | ur-bis); ait as two short syllables (a monosyllabic ait would also give a valid line, same other quantities). The scanner split Ae and made a dactyl A-e-ne.

1.446.why: Carrier line: scanned by hand and found correct as the scanner reads it (Hic tem | plum Iū | nō(ni) in | gens Sī | dō-ni-a | Dī-do; -ni elided into in-, Iū- with consonantal I). It is listed only because 446 shares a unit with the unresolved 448, and the build drops the scanner's output for a whole unit when one of its lines is UNRESOLVED.

1.447.why: dōnis: dōnum has long ō and the ablative plural -īs is long; ŏpŭlentum is short-short-long (con-dē | bat dō | nis o-pu | len(tum) et | nū-mi-ne | dī-vae). The scanner made do-nis short-short and o-pu long-long.

1.448.why: Hypermetric line: ae-re-a | cui gra-di | bus sur | gē-bant | lī-mi-na | nex-ae, with 15 syllables and the final -que of nexaeque elided into the initial ae- of 449 (synaphea). The scanner cannot elide across a line end and returned UNRESOLVED. aerea is ae-re-a (diphthong, from aes), cui one syllable, surgēbant with long -gē-.

1.449.why: ae-re tra | bes fo-ri | bus car | dō stri | dē-bat a | ē-nis: aere is aes (diphthong); fŏrĭbus is short-short-short; strīdēbat has long -dē-; aenis is three syllables, ă-ē-nis (contracted from ahēnus), which is what lets -bat stand short before a vowel in the fifth foot. The scanner read fo-ri-bus long-long-long and ae-nis as two syllables, a valid line with wrong quantities.

1.451.why: Ae-nē-ās: initial diphthong one syllable, -nē- long (lē-ni-it | hic pri(mum) | Ae-nē | ās spē | rā-re sa | lū-tem); -mum elided into Ae-. The scanner split Ae and read A-e-ne as a dactyl.

1.489.why: Ē-ō-ās (Eōus, Greek Ἠῷος) is three syllables with long E- and -ō-, and ăcĭēs has two shorts: Ē-ō | ās(que) ă-cĭ | ēs et | nī-grī | Mem-nŏ-nĭs | ar-ma, nigri long by position before gr. The scanner ran Eo- into one syllable and made a-ci long.

1.491.why: Penthĕsĭlēă is five syllables (Greek Πενθεσίλεια, -lē- long) and fŭrens has a short u: Pen-the-si | lē-ă-fŭ | rens me-di | īs(que) in | mī-li-bus | ar-det. The scanner made -lea one syllable by synizesis and lengthened fu-.

1.494.why: Ae-nē-ae: initial diphthong one long syllable, -nē- long, three syllables; Dardanio's -o elides into Ae-: Haec dum | Dar-da-ni(o) | Ae-nē | ae mī | ran-da vi | den-tur. The scanner split Ae and read A-e-ne as a dactyl.

1.499.why: Dīāna here has long Dī- and -ā-, and chŏrōs a short cho-: e-xer | cet Dī | ā-nă-chŏ | rōs quam | mil-le se | cū-tae. The scanner had Di-a short-short and cho- long.

1.500.why: Ŏrēădĕs is four syllables (Greek Ὀρειάδες, -rē- long): hinc at(que) | hinc glo-me | ran-tur o | rē-ă-dĕs | il-la pha | re-tram. The scanner ran -rea- into one syllable and lengthened -des.

1.509.why: Ae-nē-ās: initial diphthong one long syllable, -nē- long; subito's -o elides into Ae-: cum su-bi | t(o) Ae-nē | ās con | cur-s(u) ac | cē-de-re | mag-no. The scanner split Ae and read A-e-ne as a dactyl.

1.514.why: con-iun-ge-re: the i after the prefix is consonantal (con + iungo), so con | iun-ge-re, not co-ni-un: lae-ti-ti | ā-que me | tū(que) a-vi | dī con | iun-ge-re | dex-tras. The scanner read it as a vowel.

1.522.why: rēgīna has long rē- and -gī-, vocative -a short, and nŏvam a short no-: Ō rē | gī-nă-nŏ | vam cui | con-de-re | Iup-pi-ter | ur-bem. The scanner made re-gi short and na, no long: a valid line with four wrong quantities.

1.524.why: Trōes is two syllables (Trō-ĕs, Greek nominative plural, as at 1.172 and 1.232), its -es long here by position before t; mĭsĕrī has two shorts: Trō-ēs | tē mi-se | rī ven | tīs ma-ri(a) | om-ni-a | vec-ti. The scanner made Troes one syllable and mi-se long.

1.534.why: Half-line (hemistich), one of Virgil's unfinished lines: Hīc cur | sus fŭ-ĭt, two and a half feet (– – | – ⏑ ⏑), the last syllable marked × as the end of the line. There is no hexameter to fit; the scanner returns UNRESOLVED.

1.535.why: sŭbĭtō has two shorts (its -o elides into ad-), and Ŏrīōn is three syllables with short O: cum su-bi | t(o) ad-sur | gens fluc | tū nim | bō-sus O | rī-on. The scanner made su-bi long and Orion two syllables.

1.544.why: Ae-nē-ās: initial diphthong one long syllable, -nē- long: Rex e-rat | Ae-nē | ās nō | bīs quō | ius-ti-or | al-ter. The scanner split Ae and read A-e-ne as a dactyl.

1.556.why: Ĭūlī is three syllables (Iulus, Greek Ἴουλος, always trisyllabic in Virgil, as Iulo at 1.267), not consonantal I: pon-tus ha | bet Ly-bi | ae nec | spēs iam | res-tă-Ĭ | ū-li. The scanner read Iu- as one syllable and made a spondaic fifth foot.

1.559.why: Carrier line, checked by hand: Tā-li-bus | Ī-li-o | neus cunc | tī si-mul | ō-re fre | mē-bant (Ilioneus with the Greek diphthong eu). Listed because its second unit runs on into the half-line 560, and the build gives no sc to a unit with an unresolved line.

1.560.why: Half-line (hemistich), one of Virgil's unfinished lines: Dar-dă-nĭ | dae, a dactyl and one syllable, the last marked × as the end of the line. There is no hexameter to fit; the scanner returns UNRESOLVED.

1.562.why: Teu- is one long syllable (Greek eu): Sōl-vĭ-tĕ | cōr-dĕ mĕ | tūm Teū | crī sē | clū-dĭ-tĕ | cū-rās. The scanner split Teucri into Te-u and gave tum a dactyl.

1.576.why: Aeneas is three syllables, Ae-nē-ās, not A-e-ne-as: ad-fŏ-rĕt | Aē-nē | ās Ĕ-quĭ | dem per | lī-tŏ-ră | cer-tos. The scanner's fit made the final -as short and Equidem long.

1.580.why: Aeneas is three syllables, Ae-nē-ās: et pă-tĕr | Aē-nē | ās iam | dū (dum) ē | rum-pĕ-rĕ | nū-bem. The scanner split Ae- in two (A-e-ne-as).

1.581.why: Aenean is Ae-nē-an, three syllables: ar-dē | bant Prĭ-ŏr | Aē-nē | an com | pel-lăt Ă | chā-tes. The scanner split Ae- in two (A-e-ne-an).

1.588.why: Aeneas is three syllables, Ae-nē-ās: Res-tĭ-tĭt | Aē-nē | ās cla | rā (que) in | lū-cĕ rĕ | ful-sit. The scanner split Ae- in two.

1.594.why: rēgīna has long rē- and -gī-, and ădlŏquĭtur has short lo and qui: Tum sic | rē-gī(nam) | ad lŏ-quĭ | tur cunc | tīs-quĕ rĕ | pen-te. The scanner made gi short and lo, qui long, a valid line with three wrong quantities.

1.596.why: Troius is three syllables (Trō-ĭ-ŭs), Aeneas is Ae-nē-ās, and ereptus has long ē-: Trō-ĭ-ŭs | Aē-nē | ās Lў-bĭ | cīs ē | rep-tŭs ăb | un-dis. COSTLY in the scanner, which made it Tro-ius and A-e-ne-as.

1.598.why: rēliquiās with long first syllable (as at 1.30) and four syllables, and Danaum with its two short syllables: quae nōs | rē-lĭ-quĭ | ās Dă-nă | um ter | rae-quĕ mă | ris-que. The scanner forced synizesis (reliqu-ias) and gave the line one dactyl too few.

1.611.why: Ilionea in five syllables, Ī-lĭ-ŏ-nē-ă, with the Greek -ea left unreduced and the -e- long, is the only fit that keeps the present petit short (pĕ-tĭt): Ī-lĭ-ŏ | nē-ă pĕ | tit dex | tra lae | va-que Sĕ | res-tum. The scanner made nea one syllable and gave petit a long pe-.

1.615.why: nāte has long na-, pĕrīcula has long -rī-, and tanta is neuter plural with short -a: Quis tē | nā-tĕ dĕ | ā per | tan-tă pĕ | rī-cŭ-lă | cā-sus. The scanner's fit (cost 0.6) made na short, ta and pe long: a valid line with four wrong quantities.

1.617.why: Hiatus: Dardanio is not elided before Anchisae (the long o stays long), and the line scans only so: Tūn(e) ill(e) | Aē-nē | ās quem | Dar-dă-nĭ | ō An | chī-sae. Tune and ille elide before the following vowel. The scanner (COSTLY 4.4) split Ae- in two and elided the o, making Anchisae four syllables (sa-e).

1.618.why: Simoentis is four syllables, Sĭ-mŏ-en-tis, with o and e not a diphthong, and the line is dactylic throughout: al-mă Vĕ | nus Phrў-gĭ | ī gĕ-nŭ | it Sĭ-mŏ | en-tis ăd | un-dam. The scanner took oe as a diphthong and made Si long, a valid line with wrong quantities.

1.619.why: Teu- is one long syllable (Greek eu): At (que) ĕ-quĭ | dem Teu | crum mĕ-mĭ | ni Si | dō-nă vĕ | nī-re. The scanner split Teucrum into Te-u.

1.625.why: Teu- is one long syllable (Greek eu), and ipse elides before hostis (h-): Ip(se) hos | tis Teu | cros in | sig-ni | lau-dĕ fĕ | rē-bat. The scanner split Teucros into Te-u and gave the line a spare dactyl.

1.626.why: Teu- is one long syllable (Greek eu); -que elides before ortum, -um before antiqua and Teucrorum before ab: sē (que) or | (tum) an-tī | qua Teu | crō (rum) ab | stir-pĕ vŏ | lē-bat. The scanner split Teucrorum into Te-u.

1.631.why: Aenean is three syllables, Ae-nē-an (the only fit has long an before in): Sic mĕ-mŏ | rat sĭ-mŭl | Aē-nē | an in | rē-gĭ-ă | du-cit. The scanner split Ae- in two (A-e-ne-an).

1.633.why: Carrier line, checked by hand (Nec mĭ-nŭs | in-tĕ-rĕ | ā sŏ-cĭ | is ad | lī-tŏ-ră | mit-tit). The scanner's fit is correct; the entry is needed only because this line shares a unit with the half-line 1.636, which the scanner cannot fit, and a unit with an unresolved line receives no sc at all.

1.634.why: Carrier line, checked by hand (vī-gin | tī tau | ros mag | nō (rum) hor | ren-tĭ-ă | cen-tum). The scanner's fit is correct; the entry is needed only because this line shares a unit with the half-line 1.636, which the scanner cannot fit, and a unit with an unresolved line receives no sc at all.

1.635.why: Carrier line, checked by hand (ter-gă sŭ | um pin | guis cen | tum cum | mā-trĭ-bŭs | ag-nos). The scanner's fit is correct; the entry is needed only because this line shares a unit with the half-line 1.636, which the scanner cannot fit, and a unit with an unresolved line receives no sc at all.

1.636.why: Half-line (hemistich), one of Virgil's unfinished lines: mū-nĕ-ră | laē-tĭ-tĭ | ām-quĕ dĭ- | ī, three dactyls and the long half of a fourth foot, the last syllable marked × as the end of the line. 'dii' is read as two syllables (dĭ-ī) whether it is the old genitive of dies or an alternative spelling of dei; the scanner returns UNRESOLVED.

1.643.why: Aeneas is three syllables, Ae-nē-ās, and neque elides before enim: Aē-nē | ās nĕ ĕ | nim pa-trĭ | us con | sis-tĕ-rĕ | men-tem. The scanner split Ae- in two (A-e-ne-as).

1.650.why: ornātūs has long na- and long -tus, Argīvae elides before Helenae (h-), and Helena has two short syllables: or-nā | tūs Ar | gī (vae) Hĕ-lĕ | nae quos | il-lă My | cē-nis. The scanner made na and tus short and He, le long: a valid line with four wrong quantities.

1.657.why: Cȳ-thĕ-rē-ă is four syllables (as at 1.257): At Cy-the | rē-ă-nŏ | vas ar | tes no-va | pec-to-re | ver-sat. The scanner read rea as one long syllable and gave the short no- of novas a long quantity.

1.663.why: Er-gŏ hĭs | ā-lĭ-gĕ | rum dic | tis ad | fā-tŭr Ă | mō-rem. āliger has long ā- and short -li-, -ge- (ala + gero); the scanner's elided reading (Er his a | li ge | rum dic) made li and ge long, two wrong quantities. With the true quantities the line fits only if the -o of Ergo is not elided before his (Ergo short, 15 syllables, no elision). Hand reading, flagged in review.md for the owner.

1.667.why: Aeneas is three syllables, Ae-nē-ās: Frā-tĕr ŭt | Aē-nē | ās pĕ-lă | gō tŭ-ŭs | ŏm-nĭ-ă | cir-cum. The scanner split Ae- in two (A-e-ne-as) and made a seventeen-syllable line.

1.675.why: Aeneae is Ae-nē-ae, three syllables (magn(o) elides): sed mag | Aē-nē | ae mē | cum tĕ-nĕ | ā-tŭr ă | mō-re. The scanner split Ae- in two.

1.683.why: Carrier line: scanned by hand and found correct as the scanner reads it (Tū fă-ci(em) | īl-lī | ūs noc | tem non | ăm-plĭ-ŭs | ū-nam; -em elided into illius, illīus with long ī, -us long by position before noctem). It is listed so the hand check is on record; the scanner's COSTLY report is only the two elisions.

1.686.why: rēgālis has long rē- and long -gā- (acc. pl. -līs long); lăticem is short-short: rē-gā | līs in | ter men | sās lă-tĭ | cem-que Ly | ae-um. The scanner made ga short and la-ti long (three wrong quantities).

1.690.why: Ĭūlī is three syllables (as at 1.556), so the fifth foot is a dactyl: ex-ŭ-ĭt | et gres | sū gau | dens in | cē-dĭt Ĭ | ū-li. The scanner read Iu- as one syllable with dit lengthened by position and made the fifth foot a spondee.

1.697.why: Cum vĕ-nĭt | au-lae | is iam | sē rē | gī-nă-sŭ | per-bis. venit is the present (short ĕ), the only reading that gives natural quantities: aulaeis is au-lae-is (three syllables); sē and rēgīna are long. The scanner had ve long, nit long before a vowel, and se and re short.

1.699.why: Aeneas is three syllables, Ae-nē-ās: Iam pă-tĕr | Aē-nē | ās et | iam Tro | iā-nă-iŭ | ven-tus (Troiānus has long ā). The scanner split Ae- in two and made a dactyl of the second foot.

1.709.why: Aeneae is Ae-nē-ae and Ĭūlum is three syllables (as at 1.556): Mī-rān | tur dō(na) | Aē-nē | ae mī | rān-tŭr Ĭ | ū-lum. The scanner split Ae- in two and read Iu- as consonantal, giving a spondaic fifth foot.

1.715.why: Aeneae is Ae-nē-ae (Il(le) ŭ-bĭ | com-ple(xu) | Aē-nē | ae col | lō-quĕ pĕ | pen-dit); the scanner split Ae- in two.

1.722.why: desuēta: dē- is long and the u of suē- is consonantal (suēsco = swēsco), so sue is one syllable: iam prī | dem rĕ-sĭ | des ă-nĭ | mos dē | sue-tă-que | cor-da. The scanner cut sue in two and made de short.

1.723.why: quiēs is two syllables (quĭ-ēs): Post-quam | prī-mă-quĭ | ēs ĕ-pŭ | lis men | sae-que rĕ | mō-tae. The scanner read quies as one syllable and gave the short -ma of prima a long quantity.

1.728.why: rēgīna has long rē- and long -gī-: Hic rē | gī-nă-gră | vem gem | mis au | rō-quĕ pŏ | pos-cit. The scanner made re and gi short.

1.740.why: Iopas is a Greek name with a vowel I (as Ĭūlī at 1.556), three syllables, so the fifth foot is a dactyl: post ă-lĭ | ī prŏ-cĕ | res Cĭ-thă | ra crī | nī-tŭs Ĭ | ō-pas (alii = ă-lĭ-ī; Cithara ablative, -ā long). The scanner read Io- as one syllable (consonantal I), made a spondaic fifth foot, and flagged the line COSTLY.

1.747.why: Ĭn-gĕ-mĭ | nant plau | sū Tў-rĭ | ī Trō | es-que sĕ | quun-tur: ingeminant has short ge and mi, Tyrii short Ty- (as elsewhere in the poem). The scanner made ge, mi and Ty long and the line all spondees but the fifth foot.

1.753.why: Im(mo) ă(ge) ĕt | ā prī | mā dic | hos-pĕs ŏ | rī-gĭ-nĕ | no-bis: prīma has long prī-, and origo has short ŏ- (orior). The scanner made pri short and gave hospes and o- long quantities.

1.754.why: Danaum is three syllables (Dă-nă-um, as at 1.30): in-sĭ-dĭ | ās in | quit Dă-nă | um cā | sus-que tŭ | ō-rum. The scanner took synizesis (Da-naum) and made Da long.

2.2.why: Aeneas is three syllables, Ae-nē-ās: In-dĕ tŏ | rō pă-tĕr | Aē-nē | ās sic | or-sŭs ăb | al-to. The scanner split Ae- in two (A-e-ne-as) and made a dactyl A-e-ne.

2.3.why: rēgīna keeps its long rē- and -gī-; iubes has a short iu- (as iubent 2.37); the only parse is In-fan | dum rē | gī-nă-iŭ | bēs rĕ-nŏ | vā-rĕ-dŏ | lō-rem. The scanner made re-gi short and -na long: a valid line with wrong quantities.

2.9.why: suādent: the u is consonantal (swa-), so sua- is one long syllable: prae-ci-pi | tat suā | dent-que-ca | den-ti-a | sī-de-ra | som-nos. The scanner read su-a as two shorts, with a short a (suādeō has long ā).

2.14.why: Danaum is three syllables, Dă-nă-um (not Da-naum with a diphthong), the first two short: duc-tō | rēs Dă-nă | um tot | iam lā | ben-ti-bus | an-nis. The scanner read -aum as a diphthong and lengthened Da-.

2.26.why: Teu- is one long syllable (Greek eu), and sē is long: er(go) om | nis lon | go sol | vit sē | Teu-cri-a | luc-tu, 13 syllables. The scanner split Te-u and shortened se.

2.36.why: Danaum is Dă-nă-um and the -um elides before insidias, leaving Dă-nă: aut pĕ-lă | gō Dă-nă | in-sĭ-dĭ | ās sus | pec-tă-quĕ | dō-na. The scanner kept only a long Da- and elided the whole of -naum.

2.37.why: sub-iec-tis: the i after the prefix is consonantal (sub + iacio), so sub | iec-tis, not su-bi-ec; -que elides before ūrere: prae-ci-pi | tā-re iu | bent sub | iec tis | ū-re-re | flam-mis. The scanner read the i as a vowel and added a syllable.

2.41.why: Confirmed by hand, entered only to clear the COSTLY flag: Lā-ŏ-cŏ | ōn ar | dens sum | ma dē | cur-rit ab | ar-ce. Laocoön is four syllables (Greek ω, the diaeresis); the scanner's parse was right.

2.44.why: Danaum is three syllables, Dă-nă-um: dō-nă-că | rē-rĕ-dŏ | lis Dă-nă | um sic | nō-tŭs Ŭ | li-xes. The scanner read -aum as a diphthong and lengthened Da-.

2.48.why: Teu- is one long syllable (Greek eu), nē is long and crēdite has a long cre-: aut ă-lĭ | quis lă-tĕt | er-ror ĕ | quō nē | crē-dĭ-tĕ | Teu-cri, 16 syllables. The scanner split Te-u and reversed the quantities of cre-di-te.

2.65.why: Danaum is Dă-nă-um and the -um elides before insidias: ac-ci-pe | nunc Dă-nă | in-sĭ-dĭ | as et | cri-mi(ne) ab | ū-no. The scanner kept a long Da- and elided the whole of -naum.

2.68.why: Quantities were right (cons-ti-tit | at-(que) ŏ-cŭ | lis Phrў-gĭ-(a) | ag-mĭ-nă | cir-cum | spex-it); only the syllable division of circumspexit was wrong in the scanner's output (cir-cums-pe-xit). Re-divided cir-cum-spex-it.

2.78.why: Argolicā is ablative (agreeing with gente), with Ar-gŏ-lĭ short and the final -ā long: vē(ra) in | quit nĕ-quĕ | (me) Ar-gŏ-lĭ | cā dē | gen-tĕ nĕ | gā-bo. The scanner made go- and li- long and the final -a short, a valid line with wrong quantities.

2.100.why: requiēvit is four syllables, rĕ-quĭ-ē-vit (not re-qu-ie-vit with a long re-): Nec rĕ-quĭ | ē-vĭt ĕ | nim dō | nec Cal | chan-tĕ-mĭ | nis-tro. The scanner took qui-e as one syllable and lengthened re-.

2.157.why: sacrata: sa- is long by position (short vowel before mute + liquid, as in 2.165 sacrato), -crā- is long by nature, -ta is short, and the re- of resolvere is short: fās mĭ-hĭ | Grāi-ō | rum sā | crā-tă-rĕ | sōl-vĕ-rĕ | iū-ra. 2.162.why: Danaum is three syllables, Dă-nă-um, and the -um elides before et (as at 2.36 and 1.30): ōm-nis | spēs Dă-nă | et coep | ti fī | dū-ci-a | bel-li. The scanner read -aum as a diphthong with a long Da-, and so lost a syllable.

2.164.why: Confirmed by hand (Greek name and Ulixes are blind spots), entered so the reading is on record: Tȳ-dī | dēs sĕd ĕ | nim scĕ-lĕ | rum in | ven-tŏr Ŭ | līx-ēs. Tydides can only begin with a long Ty- (the one parse that fits), the -que of scelerumque elides before inventor, and Ulixes has short U-, long -lix-. The scanner's parse is right.

2.170.why: Danaum is Dă-nă-um (not Da-naum with a diphthong) and its -um does not elide before fractae: spēs Dă-nă | um frac | tae vī | rēs ā | ver-să dĕ | ae mens. The scanner made Da- long and -naum one syllable, a line of 13 syllables instead of 14.

2.174.why: iit is read as two syllables, ĭ-ĭt (the perfect of eo, ivit with its v lost), so that the final -or of sudor stays short: sū-dŏr ĭ | it ter(que) | ip-să sŏ | lō mī | rā-bĭ-lĕ | dic-tū. The scanner took iit as one syllable and so had to make -dor long before a vowel. Doubtful point: iit as one syllable is possible elsewhere in verse, but this reading keeps every quantity natural.

2.182.why: improvisi has long pro- (prō-) and long vi- (vīsus) and its -si elides before aderunt; aderunt is the future of adsum, ădĕrunt, with a and de short; dī- of digerit is long (dīgerō): im-prō | vī ă-dĕ | runt ĭ-tă | dī-gĕ-rĭt | ō-mĭ-nă | Cal-chas. The scanner gave pro and vi short and a-de long (a valid line with wrong quantities).

2.193.why: Pelopea (Pelopēa, four syllables, long ē) loses its final -a before ad: ul(tro) Ă-sĭ | am mag | nō Pĕ-lŏ | pē(a) ad | moe-nĭ-a | bel-lo. The quantities were right; the scanner showed pea as one long syllable, which would be sung as a diphthong, not as the elision of -a.

2.195.why: Hand scan: Tā-li-bus | īn-si-di | īs per | jū-ri(que) | ār-te Si | nō-nis. Periurique has the i consonantal after the prefix (per-iūrus, pējūrus): per is long by position and the word is per-jū-ri-que, not pe-ri-ū-ri-que as the scanner had it. Same line count (15 syllables, not 16); quantities of the other words unchanged.

2.200.why: Obicitur (obiciō, ob + iaciō): the i after the prefix is consonantal, ob-ji-ci-tur, so the first syllable is ob (long by position), not o-bi with an open long o. Ŏb-ĭ-cĭ | tur mă-gĭs | at(que) im | prō-vĭ-dă | pec-tŏ-ră | tur-bat. The scanner's feet are right, its syllabification is not.

2.201.why: Flagged COSTLY; confirmed by hand, entered so the reading is on record: Lā-ŏ-cŏ | ōn duc | tus Nep | tū-nō | sōr-tĕ să | cer-dos. Laocoön is four syllables (Greek -ōn long, the diaeresis shows the split); the scanner's parse is right.

2.213.why: Flagged COSTLY; confirmed by hand: Lā-ŏ-cŏ | ōn-tă pĕ | tunt et | prī-mum | par-vă dŭ | ō-rum. Laocoönta is Greek accusative, -ōn- long, -ta short; duorum has short du-. The scanner's parse is right.

2.310.why: Deiphobi has four syllables (Greek Dēiphobos, diaeresis on the i): Dē-ĭ-phŏ-bī, then dĕdĭt, ampla, rŭīnam. Iam has consonantal i (long by position before D). The scanner read Dei as one diphthong, which gives pho- a long syllable that is short by nature.

2.339.why: Greek -eus: Rhi-peus has two syllables (eu a single long diphthong), so Rhipeus fills os Rhī | peus et as spondees, with sē long by nature, māximus, and the dactyls se-so-ci and ma-xi-mus. The scanner split eu into e-u (Rhi-pe-us) and made final -us long before et, which is impossible.

2.366.why: sōlī (solus has long o and the plural -ī is long), so the feet are lĭ-mĭ-na | nec sō | lī poe | nās dant | san-gui-ne | Teu-cri. The scanner had soli short-long-short (so⏑li⏑) and then split Teucri into Te-u-cri to make the line fit; eu is a single long syllable.

2.379.why: inprōvīsum has long pro and long vi (prōvidēre, prōvīsus); -um elides before as; vĕlŭtī has short ve and lu. Feet: in-pro | vi-as | pris-ve-lu | ti-qui | sen-ti-bus | an-guem (two dactyls). The scanner's fit made pro and vi short and ve and lu long.

2.389.why: Danaum is three syllables, Dă-nă-um, with the -que elided before insignia: mū-tē | mus cli-pe | os Dă-nă | um in | sig-ni-a | no-bis (two spondees, then dactyls). The scanner took synizesis (Da-naum) with a long Da- and so put os Da as a spondee.

2.394.why: Greek -eus: Rhi-peus has two syllables (eu a single long diphthong), as at 2.339: hoc Rhi | peus hoc | ip-se Dy | mas om | nis-que iu | ven-tus. The scanner split eu into e-u (Rhi-pe-us) and made Rhi short.

2.398.why: Danaum is three syllables, Dă-nă-um (as at 2.14), the -um long by position before de-: con-se-ri | mus mul | tos Dă-nă | um de | mit-ti-mus | Or-co. The scanner took synizesis (Da-naum) with a long Da-.

2.408.why: iniecit: the second i is consonantal (in + iacio, in-jē-cit, as at 2.37 and 2.200), so the word has three syllables, not four; -um of medium elides into in-: et sē | sē me-di(um) | in-jē | cit pe-ri | tū-rus in | ag-men. The scanner read i-ni-e-cit with a long initial i.

2.419.why: Greek eu: Nereus has two syllables (Nē-reus, eu a single long diphthong): spū-mĕ-ŭs | at(que) ī | mō Nē | reus ci-et | ae-quo-ra | fun-do. The scanner split eu (Ne-re-us) and made Ne- short. The i of imo must be long for the line to scan at all (the scanner assumed the same).

2.421.why: tōta (abl. with urbe) has two long syllables and ăgĭtāvĭmus has short a- and gi- (long only in -tā-): fū-di-mus | in-si-di | is tō | tā (que) a-gi | tā-vi-mus | ur-be. The scanner's parse (is to-ta | a-gi | ta-vi-mus) fits the metre but with the quantities of tota and agitavimus wrong.

2.426.why: Greek -eus: Rhi-peus has two syllables (as at 2.339 and 2.394): pro-cum | bit ca-dit | et Rhi | peus ius | tis-si-mus | u-nus. The scanner split eu (Rhi-pe-us).

2.427.why: Teu- is one long syllable (Greek eu), as at 1.299: qui fu-it | in Teu | cris et | ser-van | tis-si-mus | ae-qui. The scanner split Te-u and counted three syllables.

2.433.why: Danaum is Dă-nă-um (as at 2.162) and its -um elides before et: vi-ta | vis-se-vi | ces Dă-nă | et si | fa-ta-fu | is-sent. The scanner took synizesis (Da-naum) with a long Da-. The fourth foot needs a long si (et sī); the scanner had the same.

2.439.why: tōtā (abl. with urbe) is long-long and morerentur has short mo- and -re- (mŏrĕrentur): bel-la-fo | rent nul | li to | tā mo-re | ren-tur in | ur-be. The scanner's parse (li to-ta | mo-re | ren) had the quantities of tota and morerentur wrong.

2.444.why: obiciunt (ob + iacio): the i after the prefix is consonantal, ob-ji-ci-unt, as at 2.200. The scanner's quantities are right; its syllable division (o-bi-ci-unt) is not.

2.462.why: Danaum is three syllables, Dă-nă-um, the -um long by position before so-: et Dă-nă | um so-li | tae na | ves et A | cha-i-a | cas-tra. The scanner took synizesis (Da-naum) with a long Da-.

2.466.why: Danaum is three syllables, Dă-nă-um, the -um long by position before su-: cum so-ni | tu tra-hit | et Dă-nă | um su-per | ag-mi-na | lā-te (17 syllables). The scanner took synizesis (Da-naum) with a long Da-.

2.468.why: Half-line (hemistich), one of Virgil's unfinished lines: tē-lō(rum) | in-te-re | ā ces | sat ge-nus, four feet, the last syllable marked × as the end. The only fit needs the final -a of interea long (as in Interea at the start of lines) and sat lengthened in the arsis of the fourth foot. The scanner returns UNRESOLVED.

2.477.why: Automedon is Au-tŏ-mĕ-dōn (Greek -ων long, the middle syllables short) and ūna has a long u-; the -na elides before omnis: ar-mi-ger | Au-to-me | don u | (na) om-nis | Scy-ri-a | pu-bes. The scanner read Au-to-me-don as long-long-long-short and ūna as short.

2.495.why: Quantities, same syllable count. late has a long final -e (adverb in -ē) and loca is short-short, so the fit is: im-mis | si Dă-nă(i) | et lā | tē lŏ-că | mī-lĭ-tĕ | com-plent, with the -i of Danai elided before et. The scanner's fit (et la-te | lo-ca) had short la-, te and long lo-, ca.

2.510.why: nēquīquam is long-long-long (as the scanner itself has it at 2.515 and 2.546), with -quam elided before umeris; ŭmĕrīs is short-short-long: cir-cum | dat ne | qui(quam) u-me | ris et i | nū-ti-le | fer-rum. The scanner's fit made ne-qui short and gave umeris a long first syllable and a long me-.

2.519.why: coniunx (con + iunx): the i is consonantal, con-junx, two syllables, the first long by position. The scanner's feet and quantities are right; its syllabification (co-niunx) is not (cf. 2.200, 2.444).

2.545.why: coniecit (con + iacio): the i after the prefix is consonantal, con-jē-cit, so the word has three syllables, not four (cf. iniecit at 2.408). con-ie | cit rau | co quod | prō-ti-nus | ae-re re | pul-sum, with -cit long by position before rau-. The scanner read co-ni-e-cit as four syllables.

2.572.why: Danaum is three syllables, Dă-nă-um, with the -um elided before et (cf. 2.389, 2.398); coniugis (con + iugum) has a consonantal i, con-ju-gis. et poe | nas Dă-nă(um) | et dē | ser-tī | con-ju-gis | ī-ras. The scanner took synizesis (Da-naum) with a long Da-.

2.579.why: coniugium (con + iugum): the i after the prefix is consonantal, con-ju-gi-um. The scanner's feet and quantities are right (it read co-ni-u-gium with synizesis); only the syllabification differs (cf. 2.200, 2.444).

2.597.why: coniunx (con + iunx): the i is consonantal, so con | iunx, two syllables; the scanner read co-ni-unx, with short co- and ni-, and added a syllable. The line is: lī-quĕ-rĭs | An-chī | sēn sŭ-pĕ | ret con | iunx-nĕ Crĕ | ü-sa (perfect līqui with long ī; Creüsa is Cre-ü-sa).

2.605.why: Wrong quantities in the scanner's fit (cost 0.0, so no flag). mortālīs has long ā and long -īs (accusative plural, mortālis = mortālēs), hebetat has short he- and be-: mor-tā | līs hĕ-bĕ | tat vī | sus tĭ-bĕt | ū-mĭ-dă | cir-cum. The scanner had mor-tă-lĭs | hē-bē | tat vī: ta and lis short, he and be long.

2.608.why: dis-iectas: the i after the prefix is consonantal (dis + iacio), so dis | iec | tas, not di-si-ec-tas; the scanner read the i as a vowel and fused si+e by synizesis (cost 1.8). Quantities unchanged (all three syllables long): hic ŭ-bĭ | dis-iec | tas mo | les ā | vol-să-quĕ | sa-xis.

2.623.why: Half-line (hemistich), one of Virgil's unfinished lines: nū-mĭ-nă | măg-nă dĕ | um, two dactyls and one syllable (– ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | ×), deum read as two syllables (dĕ-um). There is no hexameter to fit; the scanner returns UNRESOLVED.

2.640.why: Half-line (hemistich), one of Virgil's unfinished lines: vōs ăgĭ | tāte fŭ | gam, two dactyls and one syllable (– ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | ×). There is no hexameter to fit; the scanner returns UNRESOLVED.

2.648.why: The scanner's fit (cost 0.3) shortened me and lengthened mo (dē-mō | ror ex | quo mĕ dĭ | vom pa-ter | at ho-mi | num rex): wrong quantities. Natural quantities give dē-mŏ-rŏr | ex quō | mē dī | vom pă-tĕr | at hŏ-mĭ | num rex: demoror has short mo- and short -ror (before the vowel of ex), mē is long, and divom has long dī- as at 2.602; -que of atque is elided before ho-.
